How to play

Learn the ropes

Everything you need before your first run: the controls, the classes, the lobby, and how a run ends up on the leaderboard. Short clips show each idea.

Classes

Three spells for every class

Every class has the same three spell slots, on the same controls. Only what the spells do changes from one class to another.

Attack

e.g. the Archer's arrow

Your basic hit. It costs nothing and comes back in under a second, so keep using it.

  • No mana
  • Short cooldown

Special

e.g. the Lancer's spear circle

A stronger move, often an area. It spends some mana and needs a few seconds to come back.

  • Costs mana
  • A few seconds

Ultimate

e.g. the Warrior's shield wall

Your big play: the most mana and the longest wait. Keep it for when the horde closes in.

  • Most mana
  • Longest cooldown

Reading the screen

  1. Top left. Your portrait, name and level, then your health (red) and your mana (blue). Mana refills on its own.
  2. Your spells, bottom. Attack, Special and Ultimate, with the mana cost in the corner.
  3. Cooldown. A red sweep turns clockwise over the slot until the spell is ready again.
  4. Not enough mana. The icon fades. Try anyway and a warning pops over your character.
  5. Dodges. A small bar under your feet, one segment per dodge. It shows while one is refilling.
  6. XP. The golden bar along the bottom fills as the team kills enemies.
Before a run

The lobby

Every session starts on a small island with your party. Walk up to a character and press E to open its menu.

Customize

Pick your class and your color, and swap the variants of your three spells. A preview shows your character.

Game modes

Choose Solo, Coop, 2v2 or 3v1 (coming soon), the biome and friendly fire, then press Play. Everyone in the party confirms they are ready.

Upgrades

Spend the gold earned in runs on permanent bonuses, up to level 10 each. They apply to every run, in every mode.

Leaderboards

The best runs of each mode, and your own rank. The same boards are on the website.

Three training dummies wait near the castle: try your spells on them. In the lobby, nobody stays down: a downed player gets back up after 5 s.

How a run goes

  1. 1

    Waves

    Enemies come in waves. Clear one and the next comes early.

  2. 2

    Level up

    Every kill gives XP. When the bar is full, the game pauses: pick one bonus out of three.

  3. 3

    The boss

    After a few minutes, the whole party is taken to the boss arena.

  4. 4

    Down? You're a pig

    A downed player turns into a pig. An ally walks up, presses E and rides it until the bar fills: you are back.

  5. 5

    End of the run

    The run ends when everyone is down or the boss falls. You get your score, your place on the leaderboard, and gold.

Progression

XP, gold and the leaderboard

XP, during a run

Each enemy is worth some XP. The team shares one bar: level 2 takes 50 XP, then each level takes 25 more. With more players, each level asks for more XP, so it is never easier in a group.

Each level-up lets you pick one of three bonuses: more health, damage, speed and so on.

  • Level 250 XP
  • Each next level+25 XP
  • In a team of N players× N

Every tenth level is special: rarer bonuses like Extra Life, Lifesteal, Critical Hit or an extra dash. XP and levels start over at every run.

The score

  • Each enemy killedits value
  • Each wave reached+100
  • The boss+10 000

Each mode has its own leaderboard: the top runs and your rank, with the players, the wave, the time and the score. You can also filter by class.

Gold and upgrades

At the end of a run, your score turns into gold: 1 gold for every 1,000 points. Gold stays on your account.

Spend it with the Upgrades character in the lobby. Each upgrade makes one of the ten stats a bit better at the start of every run, in every mode, up to level 10.

  • Level 130 gold
  • Each next level+30 gold
  • Level 10300 gold

Upgrades are what you keep between runs, and they show on your profile.
